svg.aria-label: Content-adaptive KV caching: variable per-frame token counts are cut into fixed 196-token blocks, decoupling cache block index from frame index, with a ledger that preserves frame addressability and a three-tier store whose retrieval budget covers a content-determined span of video.
svg.title: Content-Adaptive KV Caching
svg.desc: Six-stage pipeline. Frames are encoded to 196 tokens each, StreamPrune keeps a variable count per frame, the stream is cut into fixed 196-token blocks independent of frame boundaries, a frame-token-count ledger reconstructs the frame-to-block map, blocks are stored across GPU local window, CPU pinned memory and a GPU LRU cache, and retrieval selects a fixed number of blocks that now covers a content-determined span of video time.

g.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

text.font-family: IBM Plex Serif, Georgia, serif

g.text: A cache block stops being a unit of time and becomes a unit of information. LLaVA-OneVision-7B + ReKV, fp16, n_local 15000, retrieve_size 64.

g.text: dist[p] = 1 - cos( f_t[p], ref[p] ) keep[p] = dist[p] > tau
ref[p] <- f_t[p] where keep (dropped positions keep their ref)

g.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

text.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: CUT — TOKEN AXIS: THE STORE COUNTS TOKENS, NEVER FRAMES
f3, f4 emit nothing — no width in the stream at all

g.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: held back, prepended to the next chunk — embeddings, not KV
Blocks are cut by counting 196 tokens off the stream (ContextManager._append_global). Frame boundaries are invisible to it — so B1 alone absorbs f1 through f6,
while f0 needs a whole block to itself. The store requires whole blocks (three asserts), so the tail remainder R waits in _pending_embeds rather than being padded.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: SPAN — TIME AXIS: THE SAME TEN FRAMES, THE SAME CACHE BUDGET

g.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: BASELINE — block index IS frame index: 10 blocks, each covering exactly 1 frame
CONTENT-ADAPTIVE — 3 blocks cover the same 10 frames: 1 frame where it is busy, 6 where it is static
spans overlap on purpose: f6 and f7 each straddle a cut, so both blocks genuinely hold part of them.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: LEDGER — ONE ARRAY RESTORES EXACT FRAME ADDRESSABILITY
Everything below is derived from one list, frame_token_counts, appended once per frame. No frame index is ever assumed equal to a block index again.

g.text: * carrier rule — a frame that emitted nothing is not missing from memory. It was dropped because an earlier token already represents it to within tau, so it maps to
that token's block: carrier = (start - 1) // 196 = 239 // 196 = B1. Mapping it to nothing would make a long static stretch unretrievable — exactly backwards.

g.text: TIER 2 · CPU PINNED — every block, forever

text.font-family: IBM Plex Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: mean over the block's 196 GQA-expanded keys · 7 KiB / block / layer
One block is always 196 tokens and always 10.72 MiB — but no longer always one frame.
The bytes are fixed; the amount of video time they buy is decided by the content.
Same allocation, same code path, same asserts — only the frame-to-block relation changed.
